title: Repeated holdout validation for weighted quantile sum regression.
ehr_evidence: Using data from 718 mother-child pairs in the Swedish Environmental Longitudinal, Mother and Child, Asthma and Allergy (SELMA) study, we assessed the association between prenatal exposure to 26 endocrine disrupting chemicals and child Intelligence Quotient (IQ).
summary: Methodological paper demonstrating repeated holdout validation for weighted quantile sum regression using SELMA cohort data to assess prenatal chemical mixture exposure and child IQ.
key_findings: WQS index estimate was significant when all data was used (β = -2.2, CI = -3.43, -0.98), but attenuated and nonsignificant using repeated holdout validation (β = -0.82, CI = -2.11, 0.45).
DPHP had the second highest mean weight (10%) but seven of 100 repetitions were below the chemical of concern threshold.
Triclosan mean weight was 3% but 26% of repetitions had weights above the threshold.
captured_features: prenatal exposure to 26 endocrine disrupting chemicals
study_design: methodological demonstration using a prospective birth cohort
limitations: computationally intensive (100 times longer than typical WQS)
finite sample sizes may limit stability
training-test split percentages are somewhat arbitrary
potential for random error or unmeasured confounding
